article.headline: Liam Martin storms home in 84 seconds as Australia leads World Cup
article.summary: Australia established an early six-point lead against New Zealand in the 2026 Men's Rugby League World Cup final in Brisbane.
article.body:
Liam Martin surged through the opposition defense to score the opening try just 84 seconds after kick-off at Suncorp Stadium. Cameron Munster successfully converted the play to secure a six-point advantage for the holders, forcing New Zealand to chase the game from the opening moments. This lightning-fast start provides the Kangaroos with a significant psychological edge in their quest to retain the world title in Brisbane.

Following this early breakthrough, the final remains a high-stakes encounter under official NRL rules, featuring six-player interchange benches. The match carries immense weight for both nations, as the Kangaroos look to build on the momentum of their 2022 World Cup success. For spectators and fans, the intensity of these opening exchanges signals a battle between two highly disciplined squads, with New Zealand needing to overcome an early deficit to remain in contention for the trophy.

Team rosters underwent last-minute adjustments prior to the match. Australia made a tactical shift by moving Keaon Koloamatangi into the starting side and shifting Pat Carrigan to the bench, while James Tedesco joined the interchange following Latrell Mitchell’s withdrawal due to illness. The Australian lineup maintains continuity, with eight players returning from the 2022 final victory against Samoa. Meanwhile, New Zealand coach Stacey Jones confirmed that prop Naufahu Whyte and playmaker Kodi Nikorima were cleared to compete despite injury concerns earlier in the week. The Kiwis also welcomed back winger Ronaldo Mulitalo, who returned from a one-match suspension following his high shot against Fiji.

The tournament finale at Suncorp Stadium concludes a grueling schedule for both teams, with the match officials enforcing strict adherence to NRL protocols regarding player usage on the interchange bench.

article.headline: Jillaroos storm to fourth straight World Cup title routing Kiwi Ferns 34-10
article.summary: The Australian Jillaroos secured their fourth consecutive Rugby League World Cup title after a dominant 34-10 victory over the Kiwi Ferns at Suncorp Stadium.
article.body:
Jamie Chapman finished her tournament run with 13 tries, cementing her status with a first-half hat-trick during the final at Suncorp Stadium. The Jillaroos reached a 24-0 lead by the midpoint of the first half, aided by a drinks break called due to Brisbane's stifling heat. This rapid offensive start left the Kiwi Ferns struggling to recover as Australia established complete control before the interval.

The victory marks a period of dominance for the Australian side, maintaining an unbroken streak of four world championship wins. For fans of the sport and the players involved, the match showcased the widening gap in competitive intensity as the Jillaroos utilized wide-field play to dismantle the New Zealand defense throughout the opening 40 minutes.

According to NRL.com, the scoring barrage included a 70-metre solo effort from centre Jess Sergis and a decisive combination between Tamika Upton and Abbi Church on the right edge. Chapman’s performance was highlighted by an acrobatic 15th-minute dive and a powerhouse 70-metre charge in the 29th minute. While the Kiwi Ferns attempted to mount a response in the latter stages of the opening half, Australian fullback Tamika Upton ensured the team went into the break with a commanding 34-6 lead. The Guardian noted that the second half saw the Ferns attempting to make post-contact metres, yet the early damage proved insurmountable for the New Zealand side.

Following this win, the Australian Jillaroos further extend their record as the most successful nation in the history of the women's tournament. The result confirms Australia's continued top-tier status in women's rugby league international competition.

article.headline: 3.4 Magnitude Earthquake Shakes Northern Utah Residents in Weber and Davis Counties
article.summary: A 3.4 magnitude earthquake struck near Huntsville on Saturday at 6:40 p.m., prompting hundreds of reports of light shaking.
article.body:
More than 310 people reported feeling the tremors by 9:15 p.m., as the ground moved in Weber and Davis counties. While an earthquake of this magnitude often goes unnoticed by those nearby, residents across a wide area felt the impact of the late-evening event. The Utah Division of Emergency Management confirmed that individuals in Ogden, east Layton, Syracuse, and as far south as Fruit Heights reached out to share their experiences of the shaking.

Understanding the frequency of such seismic events helps local communities remain prepared for geological shifts in the region. The University of Utah Seismograph Stations monitors these occurrences to refine epicenter data and maintain accurate historical records, which are essential for long-term safety awareness in the Beehive State.

According to the University of Utah Seismograph Stations, the quake occurred at 6:40 p.m. on Saturday. The U.S. Geological Survey reported the depth at approximately 3.4 miles. While sources provide differing details regarding the exact location—citing spots 7 miles southeast or northwest of Huntsville—the data confirms the minor nature of the quake. Records show that since 1981, scientists have tracked 73 earthquakes of magnitude 2 or greater within 15 miles of this epicenter. The largest recorded in that timeframe was a magnitude 3.7 event on Aug. 30, 2023.

The Utah Division of Emergency Management continues to monitor reports, though no further alerts or immediate follow-up actions have been issued following the conclusion of the seismic activity. Residents are encouraged to stay updated through official seismological channels.

article.headline: Chiefs Rule Out Star Running Back Kenneth Walker III for Week 10
article.summary: Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III is officially ruled out for Sunday following a groin injury.
article.body: Kenneth Walker III currently ranks second in the NFL with 872 rushing yards this season, serving as a primary offensive force for the Kansas City Chiefs. His absence creates a significant hole in the roster as the team moves into the second half of the 2026 season. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed that the decision to bench the fifth-year pro was made to avoid putting the player at risk after he tweaked his groin during the week. Walker did not participate in practice on the final day of the week before being officially ruled out on Saturday. The star running back currently leads the league with an average of 109.0 rushing yards per game, having recorded seven rushing touchdowns and four receiving touchdowns through eight games this year. According to NBC Sports, rookie Emmett Johnson is slated to start in his place. The injury news extends beyond the backfield as the Chiefs manage a series of health concerns. The team also ruled out offensive lineman Jaylon Moore due to an ankle injury, defensive lineman Peter Woods with a neck issue, and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott, who is dealing with a knee injury. Additionally, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane remains questionable with a shoulder injury despite participating in a full practice on Friday. Delane has not appeared in a game since the October 25 loss to the Broncos and was inactive for the two previous weeks. The organization is also managing the status of running back Jaydn Ott, who is listed as questionable while recovering from a hamstring injury. The team continues to assess these roster limitations as they prepare for their upcoming Sunday matchup.

article.headline: India collapses to 209 as Sharma and Kohli struggle in New Zealand
article.summary: New Zealand bowled out India for 209 in the fifth ODI at Bay Oval on Sunday, as key batters Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli fell early.
article.body:
India reached 209 all out during the fifth one-day international against New Zealand at Bay Oval after New Zealand captain Mitch Santner won the toss. The pitch, which held up and turned throughout the day, proved difficult for the touring side as they posted a total significantly lower than required to secure a series sweep. This batting performance followed a previous match on the same surface where India was dismissed for just 89 runs.

The early loss of Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli creates mounting pressure for the Indian lineup. Sharma managed only 7 runs before being dismissed by pacer Matt Fisher, while Kohli fell for 5 runs after attempting an ambitious slash that was caught by wicketkeeper Tim Seifert. Kohli’s performance in this series marked his third consecutive single-digit score, further extending his seven-year wait for an ODI century in SENA countries.

Despite the top-order collapse, Ishan Kishan and Axar Patel provided some stability by each scoring 46 runs. Patel's innings included five fours and a single six before he was caught by Will Young. Late resistance from Arshdeep Singh and Mohammad Siraj helped bolster the total as they combined for 26 runs in the final wicket partnership. For New Zealand, Mitch Santner claimed 3-47 while Jacob Duffy added 3-60 to dismantle the Indian innings.

India currently leads the five-match series 2-1. New Zealand requires a victory in this final encounter to prevent their first home ODI series loss in seven years. The result of this match remains pivotal for both sides as they look toward future international commitments.

According to captain Temba Bavuma, the team is focused on maintaining the high standards established during their recent successful run against Pakistan, India, and Australia. The side views these upcoming matches as a vital opportunity to continue their progression while staying firmly within the race for the 2027 World Test Championship final. Coach Shukri Conrad’s men have been looking to silence critics who previously questioned the team's credentials following their 2025 WTC title win.

Securing a series victory against an unpredictable Bangladesh side is essential for the Proteas to cement their status as a premier cricketing nation. Despite lacking the long list of legendary "superstars" that defined past South African teams, the current squad has proven its competitiveness by winning eight out of 12 matches during the previous WTC cycle. Bavuma noted that the team has taken stock of their journey thus far and remains committed to their internal processes, regardless of external skepticism from the global cricketing community.

The Proteas remain determined to prove that their past success was no fluke by focusing strictly on the task at hand. By playing effectively against the opposition in front of them, the players look to build on the momentum gained from their recent win over the Aussies. The team will prioritize consistency as they tackle the challenge posed by the home side in Bangladesh to remain in strong contention for the next championship final.

article.headline: Wales Ends 73-Year Drought With 35-28 Victory Over New Zealand
article.summary: Wales defeated New Zealand for the first time in 73 years during a match in Cardiff on 14 November 2026.
article.body:
The 14 November 2026 result at the Principality Stadium broke a 73-year wait for a win against the All Blacks, marking the first time Wales has bested the side since 19 December 1953. Prior to this, Wales had endured 34 consecutive defeats against New Zealand, and the team had recently suffered through a record-breaking streak of 18 straight Test losses over 16 months, leaving them ranked 14th in the world before this match. Captain Dewi Lake and player-of-the-match James Botham led the effort, with Wales centre Eddie James describing the result as the best day of his life.

This victory offers a potential path to stability for a national team that has struggled with financial disputes and empty stadiums since the 2023 World Cup. Coach Steve Tandy noted that while he urges caution regarding the team's long-term trajectory, the group is showing increased confidence and growth. Many of the players involved, including Lake, Jac Morgan, and Tomos Williams, have been gaining experience playing in high-level club competitions, contributing to a more mature and cohesive unit.

According to the BBC, the match saw Wales enter as the 10th-ranked team against a top-ranked New Zealand side. The Guardian reports that this performance represents a shift for a team that had previously struggled to score against top-tier opponents, including a heavy 73-0 loss to South Africa in the same stadium a year prior. Steve Tandy emphasized that the team's development over the last 12 months, specifically providing younger players the freedom to play, has been a key factor in this transformation.

article.headline: Billy Evans invites cameras home for 34 days before Elizabeth Holmes imprisonment
article.summary: Partner Billy Evans discusses his controversial portrayal in the new documentary You Can See Everything during his first television interview.
article.body: Billy Evans lived with documentary filmmakers Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder for 34 days in the weeks leading up to the moment his partner, Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, reported to prison in 2023. Reflecting on the experience, Evans acknowledged the risk of trusting someone to portray him as they saw fit, admitting he invited the cameras into his home despite the personal fallout. The documentary, titled You Can See Everything, has since gained widespread attention for its unique style and the specific way it casts Evans as a controlling and manipulative figure. While he admits the portrayal is painful, Evans maintains he is not the character depicted in the film. He stated he remains focused on living with integrity rather than reacting with anger toward the filmmakers or the project's edit. Despite being cast as a villain, Evans claims he loves the final product because it highlights the Elizabeth he knows and loves. He stated he chose to speak out now because he and Holmes learned the lesson that they cannot afford to lose their voices amidst intense public scrutiny. Evans expressed concern over threats he says have been made against his family's safety following the film's release. He continues to manage the daily realities of his family life while his partner serves her sentence. By participating in this interview, Evans hopes to counter the public perception that he is a controlling monster, instead positioning himself as a devoted partner focused on his family and his work in high-tech. His primary motivation, he said, was ensuring viewers caught a glimpse of the person he sees when he looks at Holmes, who once held the title of the world's youngest self-made female billionaire according to Forbes.

The atmosphere in Braga was set for a tribute to the retired legend, with fans holding up 'GOAT' signs and players wearing 'Ronaldo 7' shirts, but the reality on the pitch was a total dismantling of the home side. The scoreboard flashed a tribute in the seventh minute to honor the captain, yet by the 75th minute, the visitors had established a dominant 4-0 lead that silenced the home crowd.

This loss marks a difficult transition for Portugal, who are adjusting to life without their record-breaking striker. Despite the defeat, Portugal remains in a position to secure the top spot in their group, provided they can secure a result in their final upcoming fixture. For Denmark, the victory keeps their momentum alive as they trail behind the Portuguese in the group standings.

According to the BBC, the scoring started with Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, who converted a penalty just before the interval following a handball by Ruben Dias. Rasmus Hojlund then took control of the match, netting two goals in an eight-minute flurry shortly after the restart. Joachim Andersen extended the lead to four before Bernardo Silva provided a late consolation goal for the hosts in the third minute of added time.

Portugal will travel to Cardiff on Tuesday, 17 November, to face Wales, needing to avoid a loss to finish as group winners. Denmark, currently three points behind the group leaders, will host Norway on the same day in their final group stage test.

article.headline: SpaceX Starship upper stage clinches historic catch at Texas launch tower
article.summary: SpaceX successfully caught the Starship upper stage using mechanical arms at its Starbase facility after a 14-orbit test flight.
article.body:
The massive upper stage of the Starship rocket circled the Earth 14 times before descending to land on the mechanical arms, nicknamed chopsticks, at the SpaceX facility in Starbase, Texas. This achievement marks the first time the company has successfully captured the upper portion of the rocket after returning from orbit. Following the catch, Elon Musk inspected the returned spacecraft and posted a video of the hardware on X.

The ability to catch and reuse both the booster and the upper stage is vital for SpaceX to reach its goal of making Starship a fully reusable transportation system. This technology is essential for the company to expand its Starlink satellite internet network, which currently serves as a primary profit center, and to fulfill future contracts for NASA to transport cargo and astronauts to the lunar surface. The company maintains long-term goals of utilizing the rocket to colonize Mars.

Test Flight 15 proved to be the most ambitious mission for the company to date as it attempted to catch both the booster and the upper stage. While the upper stage recovery was successful on Saturday, the booster recovery attempt failed on Friday, leading to an explosion as the booster diverted to an offshore splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico. During the mission, SpaceX also deployed 26 of its newest Starlink v3 satellites. During the launch process on Friday, the Hawaii Department of Transportation briefly paused certain West Coast flights due to potential debris, while the FAA implemented a temporary nationwide ground stop caused by telecommunications system failures. Both restrictions have since been lifted by authorities.

article.headline: India Stuns Pakistan With Last-Ball Victory In U-19 Asia Cup Final
article.summary: India clinched the U-19 Asia Cup title by chasing down a 338-run target with one wicket remaining on the final delivery in Muscat.
article.body:
Needing eight runs from the final over, Mohit Ulva struck a boundary off the last ball to seal a dramatic win against Pakistan at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground. Ulva finished unbeaten on 49 off 26 deliveries, securing the championship for India after a high-stakes 50-over battle.

The victory marks a significant turnaround for the Indian side, which appeared headed for defeat at 252 for eight in the 42nd over. This result carries weight as it denies Pakistan a successful title defense, ending the tournament for the previously unbeaten defending champions.

According to Dawn, Pakistan set a daunting target of 337 for nine, fueled by a century from Usman Khan and solid half-centuries from Abdul Qadir and Farhan Yousaf. India’s pursuit began with a 95-run opening partnership between captain Lakshya Raichandani, who scored 80, and Aaryavir Sehwag, who added 58. Despite regular wickets by Pakistani bowlers Rizwanullah and Niqab Shafiq, Manal Chauhan’s quick 47 kept the pressure on. The final shift came when Ulva and Chigurupati Venkata combined for an unbroken 30-run stand to reach the winning total of 339 for nine.

Following the final, pundits Dinesh Karthik and Murali Kartik highlighted the performance on Cricbuzz Live, noting that the victory underscores the current depth of young talent emerging within the Indian cricket system.

news.og_title: Rep.-elect Don Leonard Says Senior Dems Threatened to Make His Life “Living Hell” over Jeffries Vote
news.og_desc:
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries is under fire after 11 Democrats failed to show for a procedural vote on Tuesday as the House narrowly failed to advance the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Several of the absent Democrats reportedly got caught in traffic on the way to the Capitol after attending an event held by the super PAC Elect Democratic Women. The Lever reports the group funneled nearly $2.4 million from AIPAC, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, into congressional races this cycle.
This comes as progressive groups are calling on congressional Democrats to challenge Jeffries’s bid to become House speaker. A Change.org petition calling on Massachusetts Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley to run for speaker has over 40,000 signatures.
On Tuesday, Democratic Congressmember-elect Don Leonard of Ohio said in a social media post that he’d met with senior House Democrats and told them he’ll only support Jeffries for House speaker on two conditions: a vote on a constitutional amendment overturning Citizens United, and an end to U.S. support for the war in Iran and aid to Israel. Leonard says, in response, the House Democrats threatened to undermine his political career.

Rep.-elect Don Leonard: “That would basically mean both making my life a living hell for the next two years here in Washington, as well as being sure to lose my election in two years. … At the end of the day, the big-D Democratic Party needs some little-D democracy, and I’m just a stubborn SOB.”
